`scripts/accessibility_packet.py`; closure record in the fleet MANIFEST round-25 entry (S035 Gate quote re-checked)

Differential counter over a frozen observation set: each of 27 registered controls must be caught (witnessed) by one of ten frozen class modules G1-G10 that never read the control registry; met at witnessed=27/27 while a placebo scores 0/27

Reads a version-1 manifest of static-host redirect and rewrite rules, resources and checks and reports, read-only and network-free, every check whose decided outcome (status, target, rewrite) differs from its independently authored expectation
Re-derives a round's own seat accounting, route receipts and time accounting from committed bytes in one command (git show and git ls-tree only) and names the contract clause each check enforces
LISTED-STEADY sitemap verdict with a selftest case

The freshness sweep's sitemapVerdict returns LISTED-STEADY when the sitemap answers 200 with the same byte count as its pin (LISTED-CHANGED otherwise), with a selftest case for it (sweep selftest 36/36 in round 52)

A mutant ladder that shows a gate is not vacuous: 13 of 18 mutant families are rejected by the round-52 wave-evidence ledger and accepted by the round-51 one, so the newer gate is measured stricter on the same inputs

The round-52 gates run a --selftest mode whose committed receipts re-derive (wave-evidence ledger 19/19, quote-truth counter 18/18, gate registry 10/10), so each gate's own fixtures are checkable from committed bytes
two gate registry rows in SKILL.md

SKILL.md carries registry rows for the wave-evidence-ledger and quote-truth-counter gates with their commands, exit semantics and pinned baseline revisions, so an agent can run both gates without oral context

Checks, over committed bytes, that every quote in an appended registry block occurs in the retained article body it is bound to (mirror-pinned rows); green at its round-55 measured revision and red on later trees by design

Counts knowledge files under corpus/knowledge that the corpus/README.md coverage-map table does not name, from committed trees; the round-55 closure re-measured 21 unnamed files at base and 0 at the measured revision
Extracts every 7-40 hex-digit commit token cited in a report and checks it against the named branch's ancestry, skipping digest fragments, so a report cannot cite a commit that is not on the branch

Re-runs every registered instrument selftest from committed bytes and tallies passed against declared counts; green at its round-56 measured revision, red later only where the audited fixtures tree moved

Checks that each quote of the Yahoo crawl-handling registry rows occurs in its retained source body over committed bytes, with 158 mirror-pinned rows; green at its round-56 measured revision only, red later by design
Runs a reference implementation inside the gate against the id resolver tool over randomised fixtures and the real revisions and fails on any disagreement (gate conditions 5 of 5 met at round 57)
Resolves S-ids cited by lane files to registry rows across the lane and sibling registries, reporting dangling, ambiguous and resolved ids with fence, non-ASCII and quoted-path handling
Counts round-57 after-receipts committed and pinned by the SCORECARD cell; green from the commit that landed the third receipt and red at the measured revision itself, as its registry row records
Checks that each quote of the Baidu dead-link registry rows occurs in its retained source body over committed bytes (158 mirror-pinned rows plus 2 adopted); green at its round-57 measured revision
Walks first-parent history over every file under every round's controls directory and fails on any receipt rewritten after commit that the round-58 ledger does not disclose
Runs the id resolver at a revision against gate-built fixture lanes with per-run fixture ids (fences, non-ASCII paths, git-quoted paths, newline paths) and needs 14 of 14 cases to pass

Re-observes each path token in corpus/knowledge/freshness-sidecar.json with an os.stat three-way result (present, absent on ENOENT or ENOTDIR, unevaluable on any other OSError) and appends dated history without altering historical citations

Binds every live gate-registry instrument to a committed receipt whose sha256, byte length and static --selftest registration re-derive from committed bytes at the measured revision (18 live instruments at round 75)

Reads a version-1 manifest of local HTML pages and reports missing or invalid hreflang tags, non-absolute alternate hrefs, duplicate pairs, extra x-default, missing self-reference and non-reciprocal targets, read-only and network-free
A frozen matrix of 20 sitemap cases (gzip, text, RSS, Atom, sitemap index and an unsupported format), each with an expect.json, plus four constant controls, scored by the round-77 matrix instrument

The offline sitemap audit also reads gzip, plain-text, RSS and Atom sitemaps and reports their finding families (gzip_invalid, text_line_not_url, text_url_not_absolute, text_empty, text_too_many_entries, feed_item_missing_link, format_unsupported)

Reads a versioned manifest, parses each local HTML page and reports the declared effective robots meta rules plus the lane's finding list, read-only and network-free; bounded to the round-78 amended case table

Reads a version-1 manifest of recorded response header fields and URLs and decides, per check, the normalized global-scope directives and per-bot scoped directive lists with closed-vocabulary findings, read-only and network-free
Keeps the receipt-rewrite disclosure current as a standing gate: every rewritten receipt under any round's controls directory must have a ledger disclosure at the measured revision
Checks that every governed receipt ledger keeps its base bytes as an exact prefix after an append, so a re-serialization that rewrites a prior byte fails

Reads the previous round's routed-defect queue and reports each routed defect open or closed against committed evidence at a revision (a missing registry row, script or selftest receipt keeps it open); met when the queue closes

Builds three throwaway fixture repositories under the scratch root and isolates each surviving mutant of the ledger guard, passing only when all three are killed; the repositories are deleted before exit

Captures declared public surfaces once by GET (status, final URL, headers, body sha256 and bytes under an allowlist) and re-derives the offline header audit from the committed capture: receipt-to-body, declared-surface and audit-stdout equality

Compares two dated capture trees of declared surfaces and classifies every changed response header by what the change means for the served representation, printing one stable line per surface plus a summary

Decodes an ordered stdin JSON list of Referrer-Policy field values to the effective policy (W3C Referrer Policy section 8.1, S458: each recognized nonempty token replaces its predecessor, unknown tokens do not reset it, case-sensitive); not publishing approval

Computes RFC 9111 section 4.2.3 current age from supplied integer times (Date, Age, request and response times, now) with the six terms and conservative corrections; it is not a Date parser, clock or freshness-lifetime decision
Decides from a stored Vary value and stored versus presented request headers whether a stored response may be selected (RFC 9111 section 4.1), answering match or mismatch, or refusing malformed input
Scores a candidate cache-key constructor in a sandbox against the round-89 key contract with 92 clause-tagged hand cases, seeded generated cases and a refusal list; the advisory line is never scored

Decides 200, 304 or 412 for a conditional request and names the deciding precondition (If-Match, If-Unmodified-Since, If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since) over supplied method, representation and field values only

Counts mismatches between corpus/README.md Entry-table rows and committed corpus/knowledge/*.md entries (unindexed entries and dangling rows, each row needing the entry path, every source id and eight words)

Decides the revalidation exchange over supplied values: which validators to send, and after a reply whether to update the stored response (304), replace it, reuse it on a 5xx, or report cannot-revalidate; refuses malformed input
